'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**At least 50 insurgents are killed as the [[Nigerian Army]] repel drone-backed attacks on military positions in [[Borno State|Borno]] and [[Yobe State]]s. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/nigerian-army-repels-drone-backed-insurgent-attacks-2025-10-23/ (Reuters)]
*[[Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)|Israel–Hezbollah conflict]]
**Four people, including an elderly woman, are killed in a series of [[Israel]]i [[airstrike]]s in eastern and southern [[Lebanon]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/10/23/israeli-strikes-kill-four-in-new-lebanon-ceasefire-breach (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Syrian conflict (2024–present)|Syrian conflict]]
**A [[ceasefire]] is agreed between the [[Syrian Armed Forces]] and [[Firqat al-Ghuraba]], after the latter's camp was sieged yesterday in [[Harem, Syria|Harem]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20251023-syrian-forces-negotiate-truce-french-led-jihadist-group-holed-up-camp (France24)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine revises the rules for its [[Billboard Hot 100|Hot 100]] [[record chart]] and implements a maximum time spent on the list if a song drops below a certain rank, intended to shorten the age to be considered "contemporary". [https://www.npr.org/2025/10/22/g-s1-94489/billboard-hot-100-chart-changes-songs (NPR)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2025 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico]], [[Canada–United States trade relations]]
**[[United States|U.S.]] [[President of the United States|president]] [[Donald Trump]] announces all trade negotiations with [[Canada]] are "terminated" following an advertisement featuring former U.S. president [[Ronald Reagan]] released by the [[government of Ontario]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/trump-trade-negotiations-tariffs-ontario-ad-9.6951469 (CBC)]
*[[Israel–United States relations]], [[Proposed Israeli annexation of the West Bank]], [[International law and the Arab–Israeli conflict]]
**The [[United States]] rules out [[Israel]]'s plan to [[annexation|annex]] the [[West Bank]] following a [[Knesset]] vote, while several other countries also affirm their standings against the plan, calling it a violation of [[international law]]. [https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/trump-warns-israel-would-lose-all-us-support-if-it-annexes-west-bank-1.500318797 (''Gulf News'')]
*Nearly 700 foreigners have fled [[Myanmar]] and crossed into [[Thailand]] following the [[Tatmadaw]]'s raid on the [[KK Park]] [[scam center]] on Monday. Thailand detains 677 people, including 618 men and 59 women, after they cross the border into [[Tak Province]], Thailand. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/nearly-700-people-flee-thailand-after-myanmar-scam-centre-raid-2025-10-23/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2025 National Basketball Association illegal gambling prosecution]]
** More than 30 people are arrested by [[United States]] [[Law enforcement in the United States|law enforcement]] as part of an investigation into illegal [[Gambling in the United States|gambling]] linked to the [[American mafia]], including former professional [[basketball]] player [[Damon Jones]], [[Miami Heat]] player [[Terry Rozier]], and [[Portland Trail Blazers]] head coach [[Chauncey Billups]]. [https://www.reuters.com/sports/nbas-terry-rozier-chauncey-billups-arrested-sports-bet-probe-ap-reports-2025-10-23/ (Reuters)]
*[[Deportation in the second Trump administration]]
**A review conducted by [[National Public Radio]] reveals that there have been at least 20 deaths in U.S. [[Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] custody this year, making it the deadliest year since record-keeping began in 2004. [https://www.npr.org/2025/10/23/nx-s1-5538090/ice-detention-custody-immigration-arrest-enforcement-dhs-trump (NPR)]
*[[English Channel illegal migrant crossings (2018–present)|English Channel illegal migrant crossings]]
**The [[United Kingdom]] [[Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office|Foreign Office]] issues sanctions against gangs from the [[Balkans]] for facilitating [[migrant smuggling]] across the [[English Channel]] into the UK. [https://www.dw.com/en/uk-sanctions-balkans-based-migrant-smugglers/a-74464777 (DW)]
*[[Killing of Iryna Zarutska]]
**A grand jury indicts [[Decarlos Brown Jr.]], the perpetrator of the fatal stabbing of a [[Ukrainian refugee]] on a [[Charlotte Area Transit System]] train in [[Charlotte, North Carolina|Charlotte]], [[North Carolina]], United States, of [[first-degree murder]] and [[Title VIII of the Patriot Act#Attacks on mass transportation systems|causing death on a public transport system]], making him eligible for the [[Capital punishment in the United States|death penalty]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/suspect-nc-train-stabbing-ukrainian-refugee-faces-possible-death-penal-rcna239319 (NBC News)] [https://www.newsweek.com/decarlos-brown-jr-court-delay-over-iryna-zarutska-death-sparks-fury-10918963 (Newsweek)]
*A [[Courts of Northern Ireland|court]] in [[Belfast]], [[Northern Ireland]], finds a [[British Army|British soldier]] not guilty over killings on [[Bloody Sunday (1972)|Bloody Sunday]] in 1972 in [[Derry]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/northern-ireland-court-finds-british-soldier-not-guilty-bloody-sunday-killings-2025-10-23/ (Reuters)]
